title: Britain's reliance on US cloud giants alarms its politicians
key_facts: UK government spends about 1 billion pounds a year on cloud services, mainly AWS and Microsoft, which together may supply up to 80% of its purchases, per committee chair Chi Onwurah.
Onwurah says the US Cloud Act gives Washington a legal 'kill switch' and can override British data protection law.
She cited recent White House decisions to block Anthropic and OpenAI from sharing tools with Britain as a sign of the risk.
Recent contracts: HMRC gave AWS a 473 million pound 10-year deal; the Ministry of Defence signed 400 million pounds with Google Cloud; NHS trusts are moving patient records to US clouds.
AI minister Kanishka Narayan says Britain needs about six times its current power for basic needs.
France moved its health data hub from Microsoft Azure to Scaleway in April; the EU is drafting a Cloud and AI Development Act.
OVHcloud had about 1 billion euros revenue in 2025 against AWS's 128 billion dollars.
quote_evidence: "The president could kill parts of critical national infrastructure by turning it off," she said.
Onwurah said those two providers alone account for as much as 80% of cloud services bought by the British government, but officials "don't know the exact level of dependence".
All three departments said their data was safeguarded in British domiciled data centres
why_it_matters_hint: UK sovereignty worry over cloud and AI infrastructure, with no easy domestic alternative.
notes: Straits Times carries Bloomberg's story (ends with 'Bloomberg'); full text read.
